confirm.stopDescList: Deletes the RayJob CR (KubeRay cascades and reclaims the Pods) to release compute. The config is kept.
confirm.deleteDescList: This also deletes the RayJob CR, the RayCluster and all Pods.

messages.stopped: Ray job stopped (the config is kept, so you can clone it to recreate the job)

list.description: Distributed Ray training based on KubeRay (RayJob), suited to RLHF, reinforcement learning, hyperparameter search and data parallelism. The head+worker cluster is reclaimed automatically when the job finishes, and scheduling goes through Kueue.

tips.status: The RayJob's own status (jobStatus). PENDING: submitting; RUNNING: in progress; SUCCEEDED: finished successfully; FAILED: failed; STOPPED: stopped. Legacy values are also accepted: Initializing / Running / Complete / Failed / Stopped. Click the magnifier for the full status details.
tips.queueStatus: Status in the Kueue scheduling queue (native KubeRay Kueue integration).
tips.scale: Number of worker replicas × GPUs per node (the head is always 1).

detail.title: Ray Job Details

pods.title: Current Pods ({{total}})
pods.empty: No Pods yet (the RayJob was just created and has not been scheduled)

detail.monitoringBanner: GPU efficiency (SM/Tensor Core activity) / GPU memory / CPU / memory / network / EFA (node-level DCGM/cAdvisor, covering head and worker Pods) · Switch between the Job / Pod / GPUCard dimensions · Refreshes automatically every 20-30s. Metrics stop updating once the RayJob finishes and its cluster is reclaimed.
detail.rayEngineBanner: Ray engine metrics (collected from Ray :8080 by the Observability add-on): task/Actor status, logical CPU/GPU, Object Store, component CPU/memory · Refreshes automatically every 20-30s. Idle or finished jobs have no data.

basic.displayNameTooltip: A human-readable name that can be reused. The job name (K8s resource name) is derived from it by the backend plus a 10-character random suffix; the frontend does not generate it. Start with a lowercase letter, use 3-20 characters, contain only a-z, 0-9 and '-', and end with a letter or digit. Put notes in other languages such as Chinese in "Description".
basic.displayNamePattern: Must start with a lowercase letter, be 3-36 characters long, contain only a-z, 0-9 and '-', and end with a letter or digit.
basic.descriptionPlaceholder: e.g. RLHF rollout, Ray Tune hyperparameter search

image.headTooltip: The head runs on a CPU instance type, so use a CPU image (a GPU image cannot start on a CPU node without GPU drivers). The dropdown lists images under "Image" whose purpose includes training, or type a URI directly.
image.workerTooltip: Workers run on GPU instance types, so use a GPU image. The dropdown lists images under "Image" whose purpose includes training, or type a URI directly.
image.empty: No images in Image Hub. Type a URI directly, or register one under <registry>"Asset Management → Image"</registry>.
image.hint: The dropdown lists images under "Image" whose purpose includes training; you can also type any image URI.
image.required: Select or enter an image URI.

worker.heading: Worker (compute node)
worker.replicasTooltip: Number of Ray worker nodes (the head is always 1). Total Pods = 1 head + N workers.

resource.poolTooltip: Choose a GPU or CPU resource pool first. The instance type and template on the right are filtered by pool.
resource.instanceTypeTooltip: Instance types in this resource pool. The backend checks that the instance type is within your quota.
resource.instanceTypePlaceholder: Select an instance type in this resource pool
resource.noAssignedTypes: No instance types are assigned to this Workspace
resource.noTypesInPool: No instance types available in this resource pool
resource.templateTooltip: Per-node resources (GPU/CPU/memory) are governed by templates maintained by admins and cannot be entered manually.
resource.templatePlaceholder: Select a resource template (maintained by admins)
resource.noTemplates: No resource templates yet · ask a Workspace admin to create one in Admin Console → Resource Template
resource.perNodeSpecTooltip: GPU/CPU/memory are governed by the resource template; switching templates syncs them automatically.
resource.quotaOver: · over quota; it will wait for quota after you submit

launch.entryTooltip: The whole script runs as the RayJob entrypoint. You can write a single line that runs a script on FSx (for example bash /fsx/.../run.sh), or write multiple lines of commands directly. Call ray.init() in the script to connect to the cluster started by KubeRay.
launch.exampleDesc: Read-only reference · the head+worker cluster is started by KubeRay, and the script connects to it with ray.init(). You can change it to bash /fsx/.../run.sh, or paste the whole script into the launch script above.
launch.exampleScript:
#!/bin/bash
# ============================================================
# Ray training launch script · RayJob entrypoint = bash <this script>
# The head+worker cluster is already started by KubeRay; connect to it with ray.init() in the script
# ============================================================
set -e
python3 - <<'PY'
import ray
ray.init()  # Connect to the current RayJob cluster
print("cluster resources:", ray.cluster_resources())
# TODO: your distributed training (Ray Train / Tune / RLHF rollout ...)
PY
launch.envHelp: Enter your own variables, such as WANDB_PROJECT.
launch.secretHelp: Pick keys from a Secret and inject them as environment variables with the same name (values are never written into the config in plain text; they go through secretKeyRef).
launch.secretPlaceholder: Select a Secret key (= environment variable name)
launch.secretEmpty: No keys available (add one on the Secret management page first)

policy.maxRunTooltip: The job is terminated automatically when it times out (activeDeadlineSeconds).
policy.ttlTooltip: How long the CR is kept after the RayJob finishes, so you can inspect it (KubeRay requires ≥0; default 3600 = 1h).
policy.retriesTooltip: Number of retries after a RayJob-level failure (0 = no retries).

close.forbidden: You do not have permission to access this Pod
close.tooMany: Too many terminal connections (max 3 per user)

logViewer.noHead: No head Pod (the job has not started or the Pod was reclaimed). Driver logs are only available while the head Pod is running.
logViewer.driverNone: (No driver logs yet: the entrypoint has not started, or the head Pod was reclaimed)
logViewer.driverOutput: Actual entrypoint output (training / GPU / task dispatch)
logViewer.podNotRunning: This Pod is not running. Live logs are only available while the Pod is alive (log history is available in the Logs tab).
logViewer.containerSource: Source: kubectl logs --follow container stdout (cluster / daemons)
